faq.a: Kafil is associated with the Arabic form كافل, whose core sense is protector, guardian, sponsor.

faq.q: What is the origin of Kafil?
faq.a: Kafil is associated with Arabic. Kafil is Arabic كَافِل (Kāfil) 'protector, guardian, sponsor', from the root ك ف ل (k-f-l). The source gloss 'Protector, Guardian' is consistent. Same name as kafeel.
Yes — the underlying form كافل is Arabic.
Kafil can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Kafil should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.q: What does Kafil mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Kafil is rendered کافل and carries the sense کافل، محافظ، سرپرست.

faq.q: What does Kafil mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Kafil is rendered کافل and carries the sense کافل، نگهبان، سرپرست.
A romanized syllable approximation is ka-fil. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Kafil?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Kafil, kafil. Script forms are كافل, کافل, काफ़िल.

faq.q: Is Kafil a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
